wins.text: Data Center segment revenue hit a record $2.8B, up 115% YoY, with MI300 GPU quarterly revenue exceeding $1B for the first time
Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 340 bps YoY to 53%, driven by higher Data Center revenue mix approaching 50% of total sales
Client segment revenue grew 49% YoY to $1.5B; segment swung from a $69M operating loss a year ago to $89M operating income
Data Center GPU full-year 2024 revenue outlook raised to >$4.5B from prior $4.0B guide given accelerating MI300 customer deployments

EPYC enterprise sell-through increased strong double-digit percentage sequentially with new customer wins at Adobe, Boeing, Industrial Light & Magic, Optiver, and Siemens; cloud instances up 34% YoY to 900+

risks.text: Gaming segment revenue collapsed 59% YoY and 30% QoQ to $648M; semi-custom SoC demand expected to be lower in H2 vs H1 as console cycle enters year five
Embedded segment revenue down 41% YoY to $861M; recovery described as 'gradual' with only single-digit sequential growth expected in Q3
Overall AI accelerator supply chain described as 'tight and will remain tight through 2025,' including HBM and CoWoS packaging constraints
Operating expenses rose 15% YoY to $1.8B and guided to ~$1.9B in Q3, compressing operating leverage even as revenue grows
MI300 gross margin still below corporate average; accretion to corporate average is a longer-term target, not yet achieved

guidance_items.detail: Q3 2024 revenue guided to ~$6.7B ±$300M, implying ~15% sequential and ~16% YoY growth; full-year Data Center GPU revenue raised to >$4.5B from prior $4.0B
Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guided to ~53.5%, up from 53.0% in Q2
Q3 non-GAAP operating expenses ~$1.9B; non-GAAP effective tax rate ~13%; diluted share count ~1.64B
Q3 Data Center and Client segments expected to grow; Embedded up sequentially; Gaming down double-digit percentage QoQ

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Training vs. inference revenue split for MI300 and AMD's traction on the training side
Rack-level system integration gap versus primary competitor and timeline to close it
Whether the >$4.5B Data Center GPU forecast is supply-constrained vs. demand-constrained
